Subject: Request: add CloudSight as analytics subprocessor (telemetry export)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. We ran this up our internal analytics team and there is a strong ask to route anonymized runtime telemetry (latency histograms, token counts, feature flags, and aggregate anomaly signals) to a third-party analytics provider for dashboarding and longer-term retention.

The vendor is CloudSight (onboard@cloudsight.io). They do hosted metrics and event aggregation and have an integration pattern your engineering team is familiar with (s3-based ingestion). Key asks from Ardent:
- Add CloudSight to the DPA subprocessors list and allow telemetry export (non-PII) at an aggregated level.
- Retention: up to 3 years for aggregated metrics.
- Need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short data flow diagram.

Attached is a short requirements summary (req_summary.pdf). Please let us know the expected sign-off path and any product/security blockers. We are targeting a pilot in Q3, ideally starting ingestion the week of Aug 14.

Samuel
Director, Analytics
Ardent Health

Priyom / Laura,

Quick security assessment summary after an initial review of CloudSight's onboarding packet (they shared a SOC 2 cover letter and a security matrix). I attached the matrix I started (cloudsight_security_matrix.xlsx). High-level:
- SOC 2 Type II: preliminary cover letter looks ok; we need the full report or a link to their auditor's attestation.
- Data scope: they state they will only store "non-personal aggregated telemetry." We need a precise definition and a list of fields they will receive.
- KV cache / request payloads: CloudSight must never receive traces or raw request/response payloads. If the ingestion path could include KV cache snapshots (debugging) we must block that.
- Encryption & access controls: require at-rest encryption key ownership confirmation and a list of sub-subprocessors.
- Retention: 3-year retention request is long; propose we limit to 2 years for the pilot and revisit after risk review.

Required gating items before security sign-off:
1) Full SOC 2 Type II report (or SSAE attestation link) and recent penetration test summary.
2) Data dictionary showing exact telemetry fields.
3) Contract language: liability cap and a clause banning processing of request/response content (I drafted recommended snippet in proposed_dpa_snippet.docx).

If Procurement requires, we can accept a conditional clause that allows onboarding once the above are delivered and validated within a 10-business-day window.

Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:02:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: add CloudSight as analytics subprocessor (telemetry export)

Thanks — some product context / questions:

1) Telemetry shape: for Ardent's use case we can produce the following: latency percentiles, token throughput per route, error rates, feature-flag exposures, and aggregated anomaly counters. We will NOT send user-level identifiers or full request text.
2) Sampling & controls: we can implement sampling at the route level and a switch to enable/disable export per account. That requires a ~3 day change to the config plane, and we can ship it as a pilot feature flag.
3) Retention: 3 years is outside our current telemetry pipeline assumptions (we typically retain high-granularity metrics for 6 months, aggregated monthly rollups for 18 months). To support 3 years we'd either need a separate long-term storage export (S3) or accept lower-resolution rollups. Product prefers to start with 12-24 months only.
4) KV cache / raw payloads: this is a hard no — we must ensure no cache dumps or request bodies are included.

Mitigation proposal: allow onboarding under the following constraints:
- Pilot will be for aggregated metrics only (no request/response or KV snapshots).
- Export sampling and per-account toggle enabled; default off.
- Retention capped at 24 months for pilot; revisit for extension with cost/risk analysis.
- Security checks (SOC2 & data dictionary) must be satisfied.

If legal/security are aligned on the conditional language, product can commit the config changes for an Aug 14 pilot window (assuming external vendor meets gating items by Aug 6).

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:48:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: add CloudSight as analytics subprocessor (telemetry export)

I reviewed the proposed DPA snippet and the risk/control asks. Legal is fine to proceed on a conditional DPA amendment that includes the following items:
- Explicit field-level exclusions (no request text, no user identifiers, no KV cache dumps).
- Contractual requirement for SOC 2 Type II evidence within 10 business days of signature; a failure to provide will automatically revoke the subprocessor permission.
- Retention clause: pilot retention capped at 24 months; any extension requires written approval from Redwood legal and security.
- Indemnity narrow carveout limited to proven data misuse.

I'll attach the redline doc (proposed_dpa_snippet.docx) to the reply. Procurement note: procurement should coordinate a short SOW to capture the storage/export costs. If CloudSight agrees to the conditional language, we can route to DocuSign.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Samuel / Maria — thanks for the ask and the packet. We discussed internally and can provisionally onboard CloudSight under the following conditional approval path:

1) Gating deliverables from CloudSight (due by Aug 6):
   - Full SOC 2 Type II attestation or secure link to the auditor's report.
   - Data dictionary listing exact telemetry fields to be exported.
   - Confirmation that no request/response payloads, identifiers, or KV cache snapshots will be sent.
   - List of CloudSight's sub-subprocessors.

2) Contract: Redwood will issue a DPA amendment with conditional language (see attached proposed snippet). CloudSight must sign and deliver SOC 2 evidence within 10 business days post-signature or the permission is revoked.

3) Product constraints for the pilot (Aug 14 target):
   - Export limited to aggregated metrics only (latency pcts, token counts, error rates, feature exposures, anomaly counters).
   - Retention during pilot capped at 24 months; long-term retention subject to a follow-up review.
   - Export sampling & per-account switch will be enabled; default will be OFF.
